But biology is much broader than just the chemical processes that go on in plants and animals. There's also biophysics, there's the study of animal behavior, of ecosystems, of agricultural methods, of evolution, etc etc.

I would say yes. At the core, everything is really just physics. After that, we are putting physics in different frameworks (chemistry), and then looking at chemistry in a the specific context of life sciences (biology). Then you could focus biology onto the body (physiology). Then move to neuroscience, psychology, sociology, economics...
